correctness.rationale: Every finite commuting-permutation orbit is Z^2/H for a finite-index stabilizer H. The explicit quantifier-free one-variable H-test follows from HNF generators and pairwise distinct coset representatives; all nonstandard term inequalities are justified by the index. A sentence with r+1 variables witnesses r+1 distinct H-orbits when r<k. The k-pebble strategy maintains an injective matching of occupied orbits and exact relative displacements; moving a pebble leaves at most k-1 occupied orbits and truncated multiplicity supplies an unused target orbit. This preserves every function-term equality for arbitrarily many rounds. The minimal-width formula follows both directions. HNF counts sigma_1(h) period lattices of index h and the Euler product counts independent minimal multiplicities 0..k. Separate scripts corroborated 348 finite pebble comparisons, exhaustive commuting-pair isomorphism counts through size 6, and 54,114 direct formula tests across period lattices of index at most 10. No finite experiment is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: For the natural entire family of finite Z^2-actions, the theorem gives a genuinely complete all-k, unrestricted-depth invariant, exactly identifies the first variable width separating any two actions, and constructs unique smallest representatives. The index sum sigma_1(h) produces an explicit infinite Euler product enumerating logically distinct classes by minimum size; sheared period lattices contribute genuinely different types beyond separate cycle lengths of the two permutations. The precise C^1 versus FO^k gap explains a substantive logical expressiveness loss rather than a simple isolated example. No broad arbitrary-algebraic extension is asserted.
